$comment: Coresignal to CompanyEnrich V2 migration mapping. Rendered into docs/migrate-from-coresignal*.mdx by scripts/sync-migrations.mjs, which also validates every CompanyEnrich path, filter, and value against openapi/v2.json.

vendor.name: Coresignal
vendor.fieldNames: Coresignal's documentation names LinkedIn fields professional_network_*, such as professional_network_url, and the company ID company_id. Its OpenAPI specification names them linkedin_*, such as linkedin_url, and id. Field rows list both spellings. Match whichever your code reads.
vendor.scope: Covers the Multi-source Company and Employee APIs, the Contact Enrichment API, Bulk Collect, and the credit headers. Base and Clean endpoints map to the same CompanyEnrich endpoints, but their record fields are not in this mapping. Jobs, Posts, Historical Headcount, Real-time Employee, Agentic Search, and Webhooks are listed as endpoints.
vendor.paths: Endpoint paths that start with /v2/ are relative to https://api.coresignal.com/cdapi. /enrichment/contacts and /rtapi/v2/employee/scrape are relative to https://api.coresignal.com.

fidelity.renamed: Same meaning and values under a different name or label.
fidelity.transformed: Same information in a different format, casing, or structure. Convert it in code.
fidelity.lossy: Related but not equivalent. Values can differ, so check the fields your code depends on.

drop.fields: the base record always comes back. Request only the expansions for the fields your code reads.

endpoints.note: Send a bare domain, such as `stripe.com`: strip the scheme, `www.`, and any path, which Coresignal accepts. The company record is the response body on both APIs. No match returns `404` on both and is not charged. Bundles do not line up with expansions: `financial_information` fields become `financial`, and headcount fields need `workforce`. See the field mapping. Clean records use other field names, which the mapping does not cover.

drop.fields: the base record always comes back.

endpoints.note: Send the URL in the property for its network, usually `linkedinUrl`. One company per request. When several companies match, the highest-ranked one is returned. No match returns `404` and is not charged.

drop.fields: the base record always comes back.

endpoints.note: Build the URL from the shorthand name, as in `https://www.linkedin.com/company/{shorthand_name}`. When the path holds a full profile URL, send it as is. No match returns `404` and is not charged.

Coresignal IDs do not carry over. When the IDs come from a search in the same flow, the search and the collect calls become one CompanyEnrich search, because search results are full company records. For stored IDs, enrich by the stored domain, or store the CompanyEnrich `id` and use `GET /v2/companies/{companyId}`.

redesign.sort: results come in relevance order, so a sort on `_score` alone can be dropped. Sorting by `id` or by a field such as `employees_count` has no equivalent: sort in your code.

endpoints.note: Rewrite each clause. See [Translate search queries](/docs/migrate-from-coresignal-search). Coresignal returns up to 1,000 IDs per page and charges nothing for them. CompanyEnrich returns up to 100 full company records per page and charges per result. If your code collects each ID afterwards, drop the collect step. Base and Clean index fields are not in the search patterns.

redesign.sort: `sort=id` returns IDs in ascending order. Results come in relevance order, so page with the cursor and sort in your code if the order matters.

endpoints.note: Rewrite each parameter, and turn each `exclude_` parameter into `notIn` on the same filter. See [Translate search queries](/docs/migrate-from-coresignal-search). If your code collects each ID afterwards, drop the collect step.

Clauses translate as for `POST /v2/company_multi_source/search/es_dsl`. The field this endpoint expands, `active_job_postings.job_posting_title`, has no equivalent, because CompanyEnrich has no job postings. The response's `metadata` block has no counterpart.

redesign.page: previews return one page of up to 25 companies. For more, run a search.

endpoints.note: Returns up to 25 company summaries, each with `id`, `name`, `logoUrl`, `industry`, and `updatedAt`, and the `total` number of matches, with no score per record. Does not consume credits, and needs a plan that includes previews.
Free. Search responses carry no total, so send the same filter to the count endpoint. `x-total-pages` has no counterpart: divide `total` by your page size.

redesign.company_id: Coresignal IDs do not carry over. Send the company's `domain`, or its CompanyEnrich `id`.

endpoints.note: Returns the observed employee count and department headcounts, with the latest 12 months of history under `history`. Pass `nextCursor` for each earlier 12 months. See the Historical Headcount API rows in the field mapping. Follower counts have no equivalent.
Coresignal IDs do not carry over. For stored records, send their domains to `POST /v2/companies/enrich/bulk`, up to 10,000 per job, or to `POST /v2/companies/enrich/batch`, up to 50 per request.

redesign.webhook_url: there are no webhooks. Poll `GET /v2/batches/{id}` until the export completes.

endpoints.note: Exports the results of a search as a background job, up to `limit`, which cannot exceed your plan's search limit. The response holds an `id` in place of `request_id`. Download the records as JSON, NDJSON, or CSV from `GET /v2/companies/search/export/{id}/results`. Each page of the export is charged as a search.

No person lookup by profile URL. With a work email, use `POST /v2/people/enrich`. Without one, search by name at the employer's domain with `POST /v2/people/search`, which returns candidates without a confidence score.
No person lookup by profile URL or shorthand name. See the row above.

Coresignal IDs do not carry over. When the IDs come from a search in the same flow, the search and the collect calls become one CompanyEnrich people search, because search results are full person records. For stored IDs there is no equivalent. Store the CompanyEnrich person `id` and use `GET /v2/people/{personId}`.

redesign.sort: results come in relevance order, so a sort on `_score` alone can be dropped. Sorting by `id` or by another field has no equivalent: sort in your code.

endpoints.note: Rewrite person clauses as `filter` and employer clauses as a `company` query. See [Translate search queries](/docs/migrate-from-coresignal-search#people-search-patterns). Results are full person records, so drop any collect step on the IDs. Base and Clean index fields are not in the search patterns.

redesign.sort: `sort=id` returns IDs in ascending order. Results come in relevance order, so page with the cursor and sort in your code if the order matters.

endpoints.note: Rewrite person parameters as `filter` and employer parameters as a `company` query, and turn each `exclude_` parameter into `notIn` on the same filter. Results are full person records, so drop any collect step on the IDs.

redesign.match_phrase: on `active_experience_title`, `experience.position_title`, or `headline`, Coresignal adds titles with the same meaning. CompanyEnrich `position` matches the phrase inside titles, without synonyms. List the title variants in `position`, or send a `semantic.query`.

endpoints.note: Other clauses translate as for `POST /v2/employee_multi_source/search/es_dsl`. The response's `metadata` block has no counterpart.

redesign.page: previews return one page of up to 10 people. For more, run a search.

endpoints.note: Returns up to 10 person summaries, each with `id`, `name`, `position`, `department`, and `experiences`, and the `total` number of matches, with no score per record. Does not consume credits, and needs a plan that includes previews.
Free. Search responses carry no total.

Takes a CompanyEnrich person ID, not a Coresignal employee ID. After a people search or `POST /v2/people/enrich`, pass each person's `id`, and the employer's `domain` to get the email at that company. Without `domain`, the person's current companies are tried in seniority order. A call that has only a stored Coresignal ID has no equivalent. The response has `status` and `email` at the top level, in place of `code`, `message`, and `data`: `FOUND` becomes `found` and `NOT_FOUND` becomes `not-found`. Treat `unavailable` as no email, and call again later on `pending`. Costs 10 credits only when it finds an email your account has not accessed before.
Coresignal IDs do not carry over, and there is no bulk person enrichment. Call `POST /v2/people/enrich` per work email within your rate limit, or export a people search.

redesign.webhook_url: there are no webhooks. Poll `GET /v2/batches/{id}` until the export completes.

endpoints.note: Exports the results of a people search as a background job. Download the records from `GET /v2/people/search/export/{id}/results`.
No live profile retrieval.

Poll `GET /v2/batches/{id}` until the job completes, then download the results from the job's own endpoint, such as `GET /v2/companies/search/export/{id}/results`, as JSON, NDJSON, or CSV. There are no file names to list. List jobs with `GET /v2/batches` and cancel one with `POST /v2/batches/{id}/cancel`.

drop.file_name: each job has one results endpoint, with no files to name.

endpoints.note: Free. Returns `credits.total` and `credits.used`. Each paid CompanyEnrich response also carries `x-credit-cost`, `x-credit-balance` before the request, and `x-credit-remaining` after it, so code that reads `x-credits-remaining` can read `x-credit-remaining` instead. A search sent only to read the header becomes this call.

redesign.return_data: when it is `false`, Coresignal returns a generated Elasticsearch query to run yourself. CompanyEnrich runs the search and reports the filters it inferred in `interpretation`, so there is no query to return.

endpoints.note: Returns ranked company records, with `nextCursor` for more pages, where `return_data` of `true` returns up to 20 previews. With `entity` of `auto`, pick the company or people search in your code.

redesign.return_data: when it is `false`, Coresignal returns a generated Elasticsearch query to run yourself. CompanyEnrich runs the search and reports what it inferred in `interpretation`.
